request_context.description: Seeded synthetic CSV fitted only to per-column aggregates of the supplied source; no source row is copied. Strategy fitted_gaussian_disclosed: a column whose non-blank source values all parse as numbers draws each value independently from a Gaussian with that column's source mean and standard deviation, rounded to 6 decimals and clamped to the source minimum and maximum; every other column draws independently from its disclosed value rates, so a value seen in fewer than two source rows is never emitted. Every column is generated independently of the others. The same source, seed and row count give identical bytes.
output_columns: Same column names and order as the source CSV header; the names are read from the source at run time and are not known during preparation.
Numeric columns hold independent clamped Gaussian draws: values need not be integers, unique or present in the source, so numeric identifier columns are not preserved.
Text columns hold independent draws from values seen in at least two source rows, including blank when blank is that common.
supported_requests: An exact row count up to max_rows; the plan pins it and row_count checks it.
Keeping the source column names and order: schema_columns checks it.

A broad resemblance to the source: the mean_value check compares the mean of the first numeric source column with the source mean under a fixed relative tolerance; if the source has no numeric column it is skipped, and because it is required the run then cannot be accepted.

Showing which checks passed: after generation, validation-report.json lists every check with pass, fail or skip and its measured detail, and evidence-report.md shows each recorded check with required or optional status. No new data column is needed.
Fictional, synthetic or practice records: rows are generated from aggregates rather than copied from the source; that wording alone is not a privacy guarantee.
limitations: No preservation of source identifiers, row identity, uniqueness or row order.
No cross-column correlations, dependencies, sequences or conditional structure.
Only the first numeric column's mean is measured for fidelity; other columns' distributions are not checked.
No new columns, custom thresholds, tolerances or distributions, and no output other than this scalar CSV.
No privacy, anonymity, non-disclosure or no-matching-row guarantee is made.
Not an exact reconstruction of the source; check outcomes are known only after generation and any required check can fail.
